pr_title: cryptsetup: support keyfile-timeout for using a device as the key file
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/21993

---

Didn't update tests as I cannot find existing tests for cryptsetup codes.
pr_comments:
Looks OK. 

But looking at this, I really dislike the fact this so far has been passing around the timeout as string. Instead, this should parse the timeout with parse_usec(), then pass a usec_t around, and late make a string from it via FORMAT_TIMESPAN() when we need it...

Taking unvalidated data as input and propagating it as-is to the output, sucks. We realy should parse/validate it, and then regenerate it in uniform way.

Anyway, this is an issue predating this PR. Hence I can't blame you for this, and the PR is good. But if you want extra points, it would be excellent to rework this to parse the timeout early on, and then format it back to a string where needed.

Yeah, indeed passing unparsed strings around is not that good. Looking into time-related functions in systemd, I feel that doing it correctly needs changes more than a few lines. I prefer such changes to be in another pull request.

issue_context.title: `systemd-cryptsetup`: option `keyfile-timeout=` is broken (possibly only in combination with raw device key material)
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > `systemd 249 (249.7-2-arch)`

<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released *major* systemd versions upstream! -->
<!--           If there have been multiple stable releases for that major version, please consider updating to a recent one before reporting an issue. -->
<!--           When using a distro package, please make sure that the version reported is meaningful for upstream. -->
<!-- See https://github.com/systemd/systemd-stable/releases for the list of most recent releases. -->
<!-- For older version please use distribution trackers (see https://systemd.io/CONTRIBUTING#filing-issues). -->

**Used distribution**
 > Arch Linux

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
<!-- Make sure to enclose the pasted kernel version in `backticks`, so that
     GitHub doesn't convert the `#` character typically included in it into a
     reference to old GitHub issues. -->
 > `Linux strix 5.15.8-arch1-1 #1 SMP PREEMPT Tue, 14 Dec 2021 12:28:02 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux
`

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > Waiting for `/dev/disk/by-id/key-storage` should time out after `keyfile-timeout` (e.g. 5 seconds) and a fallback passphrase entry prompt should be presented.

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > `/dev/disk/by-id/key-storage` received default timeout (90 seconds) instead and after it expired, the boot process is stuck forever because no fallback passphrase entry is offered.  Surfing through the web, there are examples where `keyfile-timeout` is claimed to be working as expected, all of them use true key file on some device (aka `/...:/...` or `/...:UUID=...` syntax) though.

**Steps to reproduce the problem**

Put something similar to `crypttab` for `initramfs`:

```
luks-xxx /dev/disk/by-id/luks-xxx /dev/disk/by-id/key-storage luks,header=/.../luks-xxx.header,keyfile-offset=1024,keyfile-size=1024,keyfile-timeout=5,timeout=0,password-echo=no
```

Have 2 key slots in LUKS2 header `/.../luks-xxx.header`: passphrase and key file that was written to `/dev/disk/by-id/key-storage`.  Try to boot with this setup, while `/dev/disk/by-id/key-storage` being unplugged.
comments:
Local reproducer (with `systemd 250 (250-292-g5f5131c)`):

```
# dd if=/dev/zero of=/crypt.img bs=1M count=32
# echo hello >/crypt.keyfile
# cryptsetup luksFormat --header /crypt.header --key-file /crypt.keyfile /crypt.img
## Add a passphrase to the next key slot
# cryptsetup luksAddKey --key-file /crypt.keyfile /crypt.header
<passphrase>
# echo "test /crypt.img /dev/disk/by-id/nonexistent-device luks,header=/crypt.header,keyfile-timeout=5" >/etc/crypttab
# systemctl daemon-reload

## Check if the device can be opened using just the passphrase
# cryptsetup luksOpen --header /crypt.header /crypt.img test
Enter passphrase for /crypt.img: 
# ls -l /dev/mapper/test 
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 7 Jan 12 17:31 /dev/mapper/test -> ../dm-0
# cryptsetup luksClose test

# timeout 20s systemctl start systemd-cryptsetup@test
# echo $?
124 (timeout)
```

As described above, the `keyfile-timeout=` is apparently applied only when the key file is defined using the *external device* syntax (`<path>:<device spec>`). When the device itself is used as a key file, the default device timeout applies.

I figured out a possible way to implement this, and I hope to discuss the approach before submitting a pull request. My branch https://github.com/yan12125/systemd/commits/device-support-keyfile-timeout involves two changes:

* Use Wants= instead of Requires= for the keyfile device if keyfile-timeout is defined. This is necessary to make cryptsetup run when the device unit fails (e.g., still not present after timeout)
* Create a drop-in file to specify the timeout

Is it a good idea?
sure, implementing `keyfile-timeout=` also if raw devices are specified certainly makes sense.
(i mean, it's already implemented for the external device syntax, so implementing it otherwise just means copying the concept for that case)
Thanks! Let me check out contribution guidelines first.
